qt: to the Council Özlem Demirel (The Left) Subject:

The employees of the security company responsible for the European Union Police Mission for the Palestinian Territories (EUPOL COPPS) have temporarily stopped working because they have not been paid. The security company’s tasks include monitoring the movements of mission members. 1.
Which security company is responsible for EUPOL COPPS and what specific tasks does it perform?
For how long and for what reason did the employees stop work?
How and for how long exactly have the security tasks been covered in the meantime?
at: (English version) to the Council Özlem Demirel (The Left) (22 January 2025) Subject: Problems with the security company responsible for EUPOL COPPS The employees of the security company responsible for the European Union Police Mission for the Palestinian Territories (EUPOL COPPS) have temporarily stopped working because they have not been paid. The security company’s tasks include monitoring the movements of mission members. 1.
Which security company is responsible for EUPOL COPPS and what specific tasks does it perform?
For how long and for what reason did the employees stop work?
How and for how long exactly have the security tasks been covered in the meantime?
Reply (7 April 2025) The Council is not involved in the negotiation of, or comments on, contracts concluded between civilian CSDP Missions, or on their behalf, and private security companies.
